---
title: "Configure experiments with Hydra"
---

Hydra gives you reusable configurations, command-line overrides and sweeps.
It calls the same training and evaluation functions as the Python API.

## Run a packaged configuration

From your [uv project](../basics/installing_metis.qmd):

```bash
uv run metis train --cfg job
uv run metis train model=mlp training.steps=1000
```

The first command shows the configuration; the second trains on the bundled
SIRDS bank. Configurations ship inside METIS, so these commands work outside its
source repository. `uv run metis-train` is an equivalent entry point.

Choose `model=mlp`, `transformer`, `flow_matching` or `itarflow`. Dimensions are
inferred from the data. For your own Parquet bank:

```bash
uv run metis train dataset=parquet dataset.path=/absolute/path/bank.parquet 'dataset.inputs=[contact_rate,recovery_rate]' 'dataset.outputs=[incidence,prevalence]'
```

Each run saves a complete model, training history, evaluation metrics and resolved
configuration in its Hydra output directory. Relative data paths resolve from
the directory where you launch the command.

## Compare settings

```bash
uv run metis train --multirun model=mlp,transformer training.learning_rate=0.001,0.0003 evaluation.partition=validation
```

This runs four experiments. Compare common original-unit validation scores,
then evaluate your chosen model on the test bank. Different model families can
use different training losses, so those losses are not a fair ranking.

With the `[plots]` extra, add `plot.enabled=true` to save a diagnostic figure.
See [model comparison](model-choice.qmd) for an executed example and
[sweeps](../sweeping/overview.qmd) for larger searches.

## Track a run {#live-tracking}

With the `[wandb]` extra installed:

```bash
uv run metis train training.steps=100 wandb.enabled=true wandb.mode=offline
```

For online tracking, authenticate with `uv run wandb login` and set
`wandb.mode=online wandb.project=my-study`. See [Weights & Biases](../sweeping/wandb.qmd)
for installation, the Python adapter and what is logged.

## Customize the experiment

`training.*` accepts the [TrainingConfig settings](api.qmd#trainingconfig),
including device, learning-rate schedule and checkpoint resume. Use
`training.device=cuda` after [CUDA setup](../basics/installing_metis.qmd#optional-cuda-setup).

Transformer and flow matching accept `model.observed_outputs=[column,...]` for
[known sequence conditioning](conditioning.qmd). Keep those columns in `dataset.outputs`.

For a custom split, a Hydra `_target_` factory can return a `DatasetSplit`.
[Hydra composition](../basics/hydra.qmd) explains custom configuration files;
[migration](migration.qmd) maps the original repository's settings to the package.
